topic: Minato only sealed half of Kurama on purpose, so the halves could reunite through Naruto
title: Minato Split Kurama So Naruto Could Finish It
description: Minato didn't just seal the Nine-Tails, he split it. Here's why that half-and-half plan pays off in chapter 643, and why it might be Minato's smartest move. Do you agree?
comment: Was Minato's plan genius, or did he gamble his son's life? Pick one.

lines.text: Minato didn't just seal the Nine-Tails. He split it in half on purpose.

shot.search: Minato Kurama Dead Demon Consuming Seal
shot.fallback: blond ninja with giant fox spirit behind him

lines.text: And I think that split is the smartest thing he ever did.
In chapter 503, Minato says the Nine-Tails is too big to seal in a baby.

shot.fallback: ninja holding a newborn in a ruined village

lines.text: So the Shinigami takes the Yin half, and Minato keeps it inside himself.
Naruto gets the Yang half, locked behind the Eight Trigrams Seal.

shot.search: Eight Trigrams Seal Naruto Yang Kurama
shot.fallback: glowing seal on a baby's stomach

lines.text: A split beast can be put back together.

shot.fallback: two halves of a fox merging

lines.text: Years later, in chapter 643, Naruto bumps fists with Minato.
Yin Kurama and Yang Kurama finally join as one.
People say Minato just got lucky.

shot.fallback: ninja couple facing a giant fox

lines.text: But Kurama itself asks Minato if he planned for his son to clean up the mess.

shot.fallback: fox speaking to a ninja in a dark space

lines.text: My read is that Minato hid a future in that seal.
And Naruto's the one who reunited it.
